req.title: Task update persists
req.statement: The system shall persist PUT changes so subsequent GET requests reflect the update.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that updates to tasks via the PUT endpoint should be persisted and reflected in subsequent GET requests. The test suite includes a positive test to verify successful updates, a negative test to handle non-existent task updates, and a boundary test to ensure updates at the edge of valid input ranges are handled correctly.

tests.name: test_update_task_success
preconditions: A task exists in the database
actions: Update the task using PUT /tasks/{task_id} with valid data
expected: Task data is updated and reflected in subsequent GET request
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Create a task to update
create_response = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Initial Task", "description": "Initial Description", "completed": False})
assert create_response.status_code == 201
created_task = create_response.json()

# Update the task
update_response = client.put(f"/tasks/{created_task['id']}", json={"title": "Updated Task", "description": "Updated Description", "completed": True})
assert update_response.status_code == 200
updated_task = update_response.json()

# Verify the update
assert updated_task['title'] == "Updated Task"
assert updated_task['description'] == "Updated Description"
assert updated_task['completed'] is True

# Fetch the task to ensure persistence
get_response = client.get(f"/tasks/{created_task['id']}")
assert get_response.status_code == 200
fetched_task = get_response.json()
assert fetched_task == updated_task

tests.name: test_update_nonexistent_task
preconditions: No task exists with the given ID
actions: Attempt to update a non-existent task using PUT /tasks/{task_id}
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Attempt to update a non-existent task
nonexistent_task_id = 9999
update_response = client.put(f"/tasks/{nonexistent_task_id}", json={"title": "Nonexistent Task", "description": "This task does not exist", "completed": False})

# Verify the response
assert update_response.status_code == 404
assert "Task with id 9999 not found" in update_response.json()['detail']

tests.name: test_update_task_boundary_title_length
preconditions: A task exists in the database
actions: Update the task using PUT /tasks/{task_id} with a title at the maximum length
expected: Task title is updated and reflected in subsequent GET request
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

# Create a task to update
create_response = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Initial Task", "description": "Initial Description", "completed": False})
assert create_response.status_code == 201
created_task = create_response.json()

# Update the task with a boundary title length
max_length_title = "T" * 100
update_response = client.put(f"/tasks/{created_task['id']}", json={"title": max_length_title, "description": "Updated Description", "completed": True})
assert update_response.status_code == 200
updated_task = update_response.json()

# Verify the update
assert updated_task['title'] == max_length_title

# Fetch the task to ensure persistence
get_response = client.get(f"/tasks/{created_task['id']}")
assert get_response.status_code == 200
fetched_task = get_response.json()
assert fetched_task['title'] == max_length_title
